title: Core of the Truehearted 10
content:
Jiang Cheng had every right to rip into him—Wei Wuxian had no defense for his own sins, and he knew it. But watching him spit that venom straight at Lan Wangji was something he could not stomach.

"Jiang Cheng, listen to yourself!" Wei Wuxian fired back. "Are you hearing the garbage coming out of your mouth right now? You’re a sect leader, for heaven's sake! Spitting foul insults at an esteemed peer right in front of Uncle Jiang’s altar—where are your manners? Where is your decency?"

He’d only meant to remind Jiang Cheng to keep a shred of basic respect, but Jiang Cheng had raw nerves for days. Hearing those words, all he caught was a thinly veiled dig that he was unfit to lead. A dark, suffocating fury instantly bruised his face, twisting his features into an uncanny mirror of Madam Yu's wrath.

"And who’s the one disrespecting my parents in front of their own memorial, huh?" Jiang Cheng snarled. "I suggest the two of you get one thing straight: whose roof you're standing under! It was bad enough pawing at each other out in the open like shameless degenerates, but dragging your filthy little circus into my family shrine, right before my parents' spirits? They watched you grow up, Wei Wuxian! I’m embarrassed for you!"

The foul accusation caught Wei Wuxian like a sucker punch, knocking the breath clean out of his lungs. Shock gave way to blinding fury. "Shut your damn mouth!"

Jiang Cheng shoved a furious finger toward the door. "Take your disgusting little freak show outside! Grope each other under a tree, do it on a boat, hug until you pass out for all I care! Just get the hell out of my home, and get out of my sight!"

Under a tree?

Wei Wuxian’s gut dropped. Did he see me fall into Lan Zhan’s arms?

His suspicion was dead on. Jiang Cheng had indeed headed out to track them down himself. Following the street vendor's pointed finger, an unbidden instinct had nudged him along the paths he knew Wei Wuxian would take. He’d caught up fast—only to stumble smack into the sight of Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji tangled beneath that tree, locked in an embrace so tight and endless it looked like they’d never let go.

A violent chill had prickled down Jiang Cheng's spine right then and there.

He’d thrown around vile insinuations about Lan Wangji and Mo Xuanyu before, sure, but those had been cheap barbs tossed out to humiliate Wei Wuxian, never genuine suspicions. He’d never in a million years imagined Wei Wuxian would actually mess around with a man. They’d grown up side by side; Wei Wuxian had never shown a lick of interest in men, spending his youth shamelessly chasing pretty girls. And Lan Wangji was even more absurd—the paragon of icy detachment, notoriously indifferent to flesh of any gender.

Yet that embrace was entirely wrong. It blew past the boundaries of brothers or friends. Looking back, it hit him all at once: ever since Wei Wuxian had walked back into this world, he and Lan Wangji had been joined at the hip, and Lan Wangji treated him with a terrifying gentleness that was night and day from his past life. Jiang Cheng had become sickeningly certain they were involved. He couldn't turn back, refused to step out and trade words, and instead shadowed them from the dark. Every touch, every glance between the two curdled sour in his eyes. The sheer shock, the bizarre wrongness, and the creeping revulsion ended up eclipsing his burning grudge.

Until Wei Wuxian dragged the man straight into the ancestral shrine. That was the spark that blew the dam, incinerating the last shred of his composure and etiquette.

Wei Wuxian swallowed down the fury burning his throat. "Jiang Wanyin... apologize. Right now."

Jiang Cheng sneered, dripping sarcasm. "Apologize? For what? Walking in on your romantic little tryst?"

"Hanguang-jun is my friend, you sick bastard! What the hell do you think we are?!" Wei Wuxian roared, shaking with rage. "I'm warning you—apologize right now before I beat your face in!"

Lan Wangji’s silhouette stiffened beside him.

Jiang Cheng scoffed openly. "A 'friend'? Well, I sure as hell haven't seen friends hold each other like that. And warning me? With what? If either of you had an ounce of shame, you wouldn't have brought your filth here in the first place—"

Catching the sudden freeze in Lan Wangji’s posture, Wei Wuxian assumed the insult had landed like a poisoned needle. Pure fury set his blood boiling; he couldn't bear to imagine what Lan Wangji was feeling beneath this humiliation. Reason vanished in a blinding heat haze, and his hand whipped out, launching a talisman clean through the air.

"Haven't you had enough?!"

The strike hit like a hammer, slamming into Jiang Cheng’s right shoulder with an explosive crack that sent him stumbling. He hadn't expected Wei Wuxian to strike first, and with his core still running on fumes, the hit struck flush. Blood blossomed across his collar. Shock flashed across Jiang Cheng’s eyes for a heartbeat before Zidian whipped from his knuckles, snarling with wild, crackling arcs of purple lightning. Bichen cleared its scabbard, deflecting the concussive lash in a shower of sparks.

The three clashed in a chaotic melee right on the shrine's steps. Scarlet veins spiderwebbed through Jiang Cheng’s eyes as he snarled like a cornered wolf, "Fine! You want to throw down, let's throw down! You think I'm afraid of the two of you?!"

They traded a flurry of frantic blows before reality crashed over Wei Wuxian like an avalanche.

This was the ancestral hall of Yunmeng Jiang. He had just been kneeling on that very mat, praying for Jiang Fengmian and Madam Yu's blessing—and now, he was standing before their memorial tablets, teaming up with Lan Wangji to beat their son half to death!

The realization hit him like an icy waterfall, and his vision flickered between blinding light and pitch black. Lan Wangji caught the shift instantly, whipping around to clamp an arm around his trembling shoulder. Jiang Cheng froze too, arresting Zidian mid-arc, his glare sharp and guarded.

"Wei Ying?!"

Lan Wangji’s deep, trembling rasp buzzed in Wei Wuxian’s ears, echoing hollowly as if underwater. He blinked, his senses scrambled. "What... what's wrong?"

He felt a warm trickle dragging down his skin. He reached up, his palm coming away slick with brilliant crimson. Vertigo pulled the ground out from under his feet as thick streams of blood dripped relentlessly from his nose and lips, spattering the flagstones.

This time, it wasn't an act.

Wei Wuxian leaned his dead weight against Lan Wangji’s arm just to stay upright. Seeing Lan Wangji’s fresh, spotless robes blooming with dark red stains from his own blood, his clumsy fingers instinctively reached out to wipe them clean, an absurd, groggy panic clutching his thoughts: Dammit... I ruined his clothes again.

"How bad is it?!" Lan Wangji demanded, panic cracking his iron composure.

Wei Wuxian’s words tumbled out in a daze, entirely unhinged from the question: "Lan Zhan... let's go."

Leave now.

And never, ever come back.

Lan Wangji didn't hesitate. "Alright."

He had zero interest in trading another blow with Jiang Cheng. Without a word, he hoisted Wei Wuxian onto his back and turned toward the gate.

Jiang Cheng stood paralyzed between horror and suspicion. Horror at the sight of Wei Wuxian bleeding from every orifice, and suspicion that this was just another elaborate scam to slip away—after all, Wei Wuxian had faked spitting blood for pranks a hundred times before. Seeing them retreat, he roared, "Hold it right there!"

Lan Wangji didn't even turn his head. "Back off!"

Bichen whipped around on the command, sweeping outward with torrential, unchecked fury. Zidian lashed out to intercept it, the twin divine weapons colliding with an ear-splitting, metallic screech that tore through the night. The violent sonic boom snuffed out the last dying ember of Wei Wuxian’s consciousness; a splitting migraine tore through his skull, his eyes rolled back, and his head slumped limp against Lan Wangji’s shoulder.

Feeling the sudden dead weight, Lan Wangji instantly broke off the clash, his hand darting to check Wei Wuxian’s breath. Deprived of its master's focus, Bichen’s guard slipped, leaving the crackling lash of Zidian surging straight for them. Jiang Cheng hadn't meant to genuinely maim Lan Wangji and frantically tried to haul the whip back, but the momentum was too violent to arrest.

Right before the strike landed, a silhouette dropped from the rafters, planting itself squarely between the two.

Crack!

Jiang Cheng focused his eyes on the interloper—and pure, unadulterated venom scorched his veins.

It was Wen Ning.

"Who gave you permission to step foot inside Lotus Pier?!" Jiang Cheng bellowed, his voice raw with fury. "How dare you!"

He could stomach anyone else, but this Wen dog had caved in Jin Zixuan's chest with bare hands, destroying his sister's happiness and carving her path to the grave. Merely looking at the monster made him want to rip it limb from limb. For this beast to dare soil the grounds of Lotus Pier was a death wish!

Weighed down by those two lives, Wen Ning had always carried a mountain of guilt, instinctively shrinking away from Jiang Cheng in terror. Yet right now, he stood firm before Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji, taking the full, searing brunt of Zidian across his chest. The lightning tore a grotesque, charred trench through his flesh, but his feet remained rooted to the stone.

Confirming that Wei Wuxian had simply passed out from exhaustion and surging rage, Lan Wangji finally pulled his eyes away.

In front of him, Wen Ning held an object aloft, thrusting it straight at Jiang Cheng’s chest.

The lightning dancing around Jiang Cheng's knuckles burned so hot it had turned blinding white, matching the murderous intent bleeding from his eyes. He let out a dark, ragged laugh. "What the hell do you think you're doing?"

Resting in Wen Ning's hands was Wei Wuxian’s spiritual sword, Suibian. Wei Wuxian had found carrying it a chore and tossed it aside, leaving it in Wen Ning’s care.

Wen Ning thrust the hilt forward. "Draw it."

His voice was dead level, his eyes unblinking—completely stripped of his usual timid stutter.

Jiang Cheng sneered, "I'm warning you: if you don't want your bones ground to dust a second time, take your filthy boots off Yunmeng soil and get the fuck out!"

Wen Ning practically slammed the hilt into his ribs, raising his voice to a command: "Draw it! Pull the steel!"

A wild, unexplainable panic flared in Jiang Cheng’s chest, making his heart hammer against his ribs. As if possessed by a phantom hand, his fingers reached out, his left hand clamping around Suibian’s hilt.

He pulled.

A blinding, pristine arc of white sword-glare cleared the ancient scabbard with a crystalline hiss!

Jiang Cheng froze, staring down at the brilliant, humming steel in his grip, his mind going dead quiet.

This blade was Suibian. Wei Wuxian’s sword. After the Siege of the Burial Mounds, it had been locked away in the Lanling Jin vaults. It had long since sealed itself; for thirteen years, not a single living soul who laid hands on that hilt had been able to budge the blade by a fraction of an inch.

So why had it slid free for him? Had the seal shattered?

"The seal isn't broken!" Wen Ning said, cutting through the silence. "It's still locked tight. Put it back and hand it to anyone else in that hall—not a single one of them will draw an inch of steel."

Jiang Cheng’s face crumbled into chaotic bewilderment. "Then why did it open for me?!"

"Because that sword," Wen Ning said softly, "recognizes you as Master Wei."

Behind them, Lan Wangji shifted the unconscious Wei Wuxian higher on his back, rising slowly to his feet.

Jiang Cheng’s voice cracked, sharp and shrill: "What do you mean it thinks I'm Wei Wuxian?! How would it know?! Why me?!"

Wen Ning's voice rose, cutting like a rusted blade:

"Because the golden core currently circulating spiritual energy through your body... belongs to him!"
